tier_rationale: Manufacturer's own product page lists a mechanical high-speed straight-stitch machine controlled by a foot pedal, a manual stitch-length dial, and physical switches for the feed dogs and needle threader, with no WiFi, Bluetooth, app, or connectivity feature mentioned. FCC sibling control confirms it directly: Juki Corporation (grantee CXJ) holds an FCC grant with a WiFi test report for a different, computerized model (HZL-UX8, FCC ID CXJ-HC501X1) explicitly identified in the filing as a 'Sewing Machine' with WLAN — but no grant exists for the TL-2000Qi.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes. The TL-2000Qi is a single-purpose straight-stitch machine: thread it, set stitch length with the mechanical dial, and run it with the foot pedal. There is no screen, no Wi-Fi, no app, and no account anywhere in its operation — every function lives in the machine's own mechanism.

repairability.notes: Sold and serviced through a network of authorized JUKI dealers; the aluminum die-cast body and mechanical drivetrain are the same category of construction as Juki's industrial machines, which are widely repaired by sewing-machine technicians.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page for the TL-2000Qi, listed under 'Mechanical & Semi Professional Sewing.' Describes foot-pedal speed control, a manual stitch-length dial (up to 6mm), a thread tension scale, a lever-operated needle threader, and physical feed-dog controls. No digital screen, WiFi, Bluetooth, or connectivity feature mentioned. JUKI suggested retail price $1,799.00, sold through authorized dealers.

FCC grant list for Juki Corporation (grantee CXJ, 24 filed grants since 1983). Establishes the sibling control: one grant (CXJ-HC501X1) is explicitly for a 'Sewing Machine' — the computerized HZL-UX8 — and includes a WiFi test report, confirming Juki files FCC grants for its connected sewing machines. No grant of any kind exists for the TL-2000Qi.

open_questions: No teardown or internal photos of the TL-2000Qi located to physically confirm the absence of a radio board, though the sibling-control evidence is strong.
Confirm whether any successor or refreshed TL-series models released after 2026 retain the same fully mechanical design.
notes: A clean example of the model-line pattern this project looks for: the same manufacturer sells a computerized, WiFi-equipped quilting machine (HZL-UX8) right alongside this mechanical long-arm model, and the FCC filing record cleanly separates the two.
